record.paper_title: Some open problems in mathematical relativity
record.original_question: What singularities can occur in solutions of the static and stationary vacuum Einstein equations, beginning with the possible singularities of the spacelike slices?

evidence.quote: Give a general discussion of the possible types of singularities which may occur for solutions to the static and stationary vacuum Einstein equations, starting with a description of the possible singularities of the spacelike slices.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider solutions of the vacuum Einstein equations $\mathrm{Ric}(g)=0$ on a 4-dimensional Lorentzian manifold $(M,g)$ that are either static (admitting a hypersurface-orthogonal timelike Killing vector field) or, more generally, stationary (admitting a timelike Killing vector field). In the static case the metric can be written, on the region where the Killing field is timelike, as $g = -V^2\, dt^2 + h$, where $h$ is a Riemannian metric on a 3-dimensional quotient manifold $\Sigma$ (a "spacelike slice") and $V>0$ satisfies $V\,\mathrm{Ric}(h)=\nabla^2 V$, $\Delta V=0$; in the stationary case one obtains an analogous quotient $(\Sigma,h)$ with additional twist data. A singularity is understood as a point or set where the metric $g$ (or, on the quotient, the data $(h,V)$ and the twist) fails to be smoothly extendible.

Provide a general classification and description of the possible types of singularities that can occur for solutions of the static and stationary vacuum Einstein equations. In particular, begin by describing the possible singularities of the spacelike slice $(\Sigma,h)$ (such as conical singularities, asymptotic ends, points where $V\to 0$ or $V\to\infty$, curvature blow-up, degenerations of the metric, struts, etc.) and then determine which of these correspond to genuine spacetime singularities of $(M,g)$ versus removable or coordinate singularities.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of giving a general classification of singularities for static and stationary vacuum Einstein solutions, beginning with singularities of the spacelike slices, remains a broad open program. While individual examples (e.g., Schwarzschild-type, Curzon, conical struts, periodic Kasner-asymptotic ends, multi-black-hole configurations) and partial results (e.g., 5-dimensional space-periodic static solutions, uniqueness theorems for stationary black holes) are known, no comprehensive classification has been established in the literature.

status_evidence.title: 5-Dimensional Space-Periodic Solutions of the Static Vacuum Einstein Equations
status_evidence.snippet: Constructs new families of space-periodic static vacuum solutions with Kasner asymptotics, indicating the singularity landscape is still being explored.
status_evidence.claim: New classes of singular static vacuum solutions are still being discovered, indicating no complete classification exists.

status_evidence.title: Stationary multiple euclidon solutions to the vacuum Einstein equations
status_evidence.snippet: Recent constructions of stationary vacuum solutions with various singular structures.
status_evidence.claim: Ongoing research into stationary vacuum singularities supports that the general classification problem remains open.

status_evidence.title: On uniqueness of stationary vacuum black holes
status_evidence.snippet: Uniqueness results for stationary vacuum black holes are partial and rely on regularity assumptions.
status_evidence.claim: Partial uniqueness/classification results exist but do not exhaust the possible singularities.
